Compares both complete fill bearings using the actual post-grade exit. Reverse grading finishes at the fill's entry end, so an ordinary sequence end anchor scores the wrong route boundary when grade return is enabled. The lower driven-metre score wins. Manual assists break ties only, because their length is already inside that score. Equal scores keep the earlier seed.

member.name: T:HaulBuilder.HaulCycleChainOptimizer
member.summary: Couples cut-to-fill ownership with the following next-cut transition. It searches the complete equal-load portfolio, swaps whole fill ledgers, and scores candidates with the production time model plus the actual routing transition model. Only compact-guidance-feasible, exactly conserved changes are accepted. Route count and every cut ownership remain fixed.

member.name: M:HaulBuilder.RunSequencer.SelectBoundedFlexibleOptions(System.Collections.Generic.List{HaulBuilder.RunSequencer.SequencedRun},System.Double)
member.summary: Retains low-cost flexible variants plus the deepest entry, exit, and combined retreats so bounded search does not discard edge clearance.

Builds a deterministic bounded flexible-endpoint sequence when subset search would grow exponentially. A small number of alternate first choices is tried only when the default greedy walk cannot finish.
Keeps only a fixed number of lowest-cost partial flexible sequences at each depth, preventing subset-state growth while avoiding greedy traps.

Exhaustively orders the already-pruned flexible endpoint options for a small run group. Connector costs are cached by endpoint pair, so the exponential portion is limited to at most 2^10 subset states rather than repeatedly invoking the geometric planner for every ordering.

Tries a bounded nearest-first set of forward-only transitions from runs which have no ordinary outbound edge. Successful costs are fed into a second exact-order pass; normal runs never pay for this search.
Builds one bounded greedy flexible order.

member.name: M:HaulBuilder.TransitPlanner.IsGrosslyDisproportionate(System.Double,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Rejects exact-pose geometry whose distance is grossly out of proportion to an already validated small-angle forward alternative.
member.remarks: The multiplicative 4× gate catches tiny near-coincident loops. The half-turn waste gate catches full-circle Dubins words on longer corridor jogs (e.g. TheShop2 route 7 fill→fill) where 2πR is only ~2–3× the straight jog and would otherwise survive the 4× test.

member.name: M:HaulBuilder.TransitPlanner.ShortAlignmentJog(HaulBuilder.ConnectorPlanner.Pose,HaulBuilder.ConnectorPlanner.Pose,System.Double,HaulBuilder.Grid)
member.summary: Uses a short forward jog when two nearby poses differ only by the small endpoint correction intentionally delegated to guidance/operator tracking. This prevents an exact-pose Dubins solution from inserting a full loop to resolve a few degrees across approximately one blade width.
member.remarks: Tolerance is 30° (not 15°) so a short corridor right-jog whose chord bears slightly off the travel heading still qualifies — TheShop2 route 7's fill→fill connector was ~28° off and otherwise fell through to a 2πR loop.
